stats.fact: Current OmniRoute README headline says the gateway connects every AI tool to 237 providers, including 90+ free tiers, through one endpoint.
The same README claims RTK + Caveman compression saves 15-95% tokens and lists 17 routing strategies.

OmniRoute's Free Tiers reference says the steady documented recurring free-token grant is about 1.54B tokens/month and first-month signup-credit total is about 2.15B tokens; the honest headline rounds this to about 1.6B and 2.1B.
The Free Tiers reference was last researched on 2026-06-17 and warns not to headline the theoretical 10B-token ceiling because it extrapolates rate limits, not guaranteed monthly grants.
GitHub API on 2026-07-10 reported diegosouzapw/OmniRoute at 14,402 stars, 2,130 forks, 281 open issues, TypeScript, MIT License, created 2026-02-13, pushed 2026-07-10.
npm registry reported omniroute latest version 3.8.46, MIT license, 285 published versions, and description 'Unified AI router with 160+ providers...'.
npm downloads API reported 58,579 downloads for omniroute from 2026-06-09 through 2026-07-08.
Docker Hub API reported diegosouzapw/omniroute as public/active with 263,015 pulls and last updated 2026-07-08.
Official omniroute.online metadata still says 236 providers, 95 MCP tools, and 17 routing strategies, so source timestamps matter when quoting counts.
OpenRouter's public models API returned 347 models, 56 provider-prefixes, and 26 zero/free-priced model entries in this research pass.
LiteLLM's GitHub repo describes itself as a Python SDK and AI Gateway/proxy for 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI or native format; GitHub API reported 53,137 stars and 9,630 forks on 2026-07-10.

LiteLLM Proxy quick-start docs claim the gateway manages unified interface, cost tracking, authentication, spend tracking, budgets, virtual keys, load balancing, and 1.5k+ requests/second in load tests.
Portkey's gateway repo describes support for routing to 1,600+ LLMs and 50+ AI guardrails; GitHub API reported 12,383 stars and 1,194 forks on 2026-07-10.
Vercel AI Gateway docs describe a unified API for hundreds of models through one endpoint with budgets, usage monitoring, load balancing, and fallbacks.

Cloudflare AI Gateway docs list provider-native integrations, unified OpenAI-compatible API, caching, spend limits, rate limiting, dynamic routing, DLP, guardrails, observability, logging, and coding-agent setup pages.

Bifrost's GitHub repo describes a Go enterprise AI gateway with 1000+ model support, adaptive load balancing, guardrails, <100 microsecond overhead at 5k RPS, and GitHub API reported 6,403 stars on 2026-07-10.

angles: Lead with the update: the assigned keyword says 231-provider gateway, but current primary sources now claim 237 providers and 90+ free tiers. Use the old number in SEO phrasing, then correct it early with a dated source note.

Differentiate OmniRoute from hosted gateways: OpenRouter/Vercel/Cloudflare are convenient hosted endpoints, while OmniRoute is local/self-hosted and optimized for draining scattered free tiers across coding agents.

Treat 'free AI gateway' as a quota orchestration claim, not a magic unlimited-LLM claim. Explain recurring grants, signup credits, no-cap providers, and why the theoretical ceiling should not be headlined.
Make coding agents the review lens: test Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, opencode, and Antigravity configuration rather than generic chat-app routing.

Turn inconsistent counts into trust: README says 237/90+, site says 236/95 MCP tools, npm says 160+ providers, older articles say 231 or 236. The review should cite dates and explain fast-moving docs.
Include a privacy and ToS section: free providers may log or train on prompts, and self-hosting routes traffic locally but upstream requests still go to selected providers.
Use competitor weakness: existing SERP pages are mostly setup notes or README mirrors. A stronger article should include hands-on setup, source-checked stats, comparison table, caveats, and verdict.
Position the technical moat around combos, fallback tiers, compression, MCP/A2A control, dashboard, and local-first deployment rather than just raw provider count.
